defendant: Union Metal Industries Corporation, 1432 Maple Avenue Northeast, Canton, OH 44705. Pleaded as a Delaware corporation licensed or registered to do business in Ohio.
agreement: A JobsOhio "Grant Agreement" dated on or about August 10, 2019, attached as Exhibit 1, and an "Amended and Restated JobsOhio Grant Agreement" dated on or about February 13, 2020, attached as Exhibit 2. The complaint refers to the two collectively as the "Grant Agreement." Three separate grants are named inside it: a JobsOhio Revitalization Grant (SFPN_2018_455827-RG), a JobsOhio Workforce Training Grant (SFPN_2018_455827-WF) and a JobsOhio Economic Development Grant (SFPN_2018_455827-ED).
program: This complaint does name programs, unlike most. It names a JobsOhio Revitalization Grant, a JobsOhio Workforce Training Grant and a JobsOhio Economic Development Grant, and gives each an internal grant number beginning SFPN_2018_455827. The amendment's stated purpose, quoted in the complaint, was to cut the Revitalization Grant from $1,000,000 to $500,000, cut the Workforce Training Grant from $250,000 to $100,000, and add a new Economic Development Grant of $650,000.
amount_sought: $1,250,000.00, plus interest including prejudgment interest, reasonable attorney fees, costs and expenses. This is the full amount of grant funds disbursed, not a prorated shortfall. JobsOhio's own two demand letters, of 2025-02-14 and 2025-07-09, had each demanded only $200,000.00. The complaint pleads that because the company did not pay the $200,000 demanded, it 'is therefore in breach of the Grant Agreement, pursuant to which Defendant is liable to JobsOhio for the full amount of the grant funds received, being $1,250,000.00.'
job_commitments: Create 250 new jobs at the Project Site (1432 Maple Avenue Northeast, Canton, Ohio 44705) with a payroll of at least $13,000,000.00; train 121 employees with a Total Training Investment of $448,643.00; and make Fixed Asset Investments at the Project Site of $2,788,000.00. Metric Evaluation Date 2021-12-31. Metric Expiration Date 2023-12-31. The amendment cut the grant amounts but, per the complaint, 'retained Defendant's obligation' to the same metrics.
shortfall: Per the company's own 2023 Annual Report, as pleaded: it 'only created 137 new jobs instead of the 250 new jobs required under the Grant Agreement, and the payroll for the new jobs created was $7,400,784.00, instead of the $13,000,000.00 payroll for new jobs required under the Grant Agreement.' The complaint does not say whether the training or fixed-asset metrics were met.
repayment_quote: Section 5, quoted at paragraph 7: "5. Metrics and Maintenance of Operations. Grantor has approved an award of financial assistance to Grantee to induce Grantee to undertake and complete the Project with the goal of attracting and retaining business opportunities for the State of Ohio that create and/or retain a significant number of jobs for Ohioans. Accordingly, achieving Grantee's Metric Commitment obligations at the Project site during the Term are essential terms of this Agreement. *** (a) Metric Commitment. Grantee must attain all Metric Commitments set forth on the first page of this Agreement no later than the Metric Evaluation Date. Once Metric Commitments have been met, Grantee shall maintain such Metric Commitments through the Metric Expiration Date. *** (c) Remedy. If Grantee fails to satisfy its obligations under Section 5(a), Section 6(b), or to maintain substantial operations at the Project site during the Term, Grantee is in default of this Agreement and Grantor may seek the remedies provided to Grantor under Section 9 of this Agreement." || Section 6(b), quoted at paragraph 8: "Annual Reports. Grantee shall submit to Grantor an annual report in the format required by Grantor (the “Annual Report”). Each Annual Report shall provide information for the applicable reporting period detailing the progress of the Project, and Metric Commitments to date. Annual Reports shall be submitted by Grantee for each calendar year (or part of a year) during the Term of this Agreement, and each Annual Report shall be received by Grantor no later than March 1 following the calendar year covered by such Annual Report. Failure by Grantee to submit any Annual Report shall be a default for which Grantor may terminate this Agreement as set forth in Section 9." || Section 9, quoted at paragraph 9: "(a) Breach. Grantee shall be deemed to be in “Breach” of this Agreement if: *** ii. Grantee fails to comply with the Metric Commitment requirements set forth in Section 5 hereof; iii. Grantee fails to timely comply with its reporting obligations under Section 6 hereof; iv. Grantee fails to maintain substantial operations at the Project Address during the Term (“substantial operations” as used herein means the Grantee's ongoing, primary business purpose or activity, and does not include a contraction or cessation of operations that lasts less than ninety (90) days); *** (b) Effect of Breach; Remedies. *** In the event of a Breach by Grantee, Grantor may terminate this Agreement and may in addition exercise one or more of the following remedies: *** (ii) Demand Repayment of Grant Funds. Grantor may demand repayment of all or a portion of Grant Funds disbursed. Grantee shall repay such Grant Funds within thirty (30) days after written demand by Grantor. (iii) Other Legal Remedies. Pursue any other legal or equitable remedies Grantor may have under this Agreement or applicable law." || Section 9(e), quoted in part at paragraph 14, for fees: Defendant is liable for "all expenses, including, without limitation, reasonable attorneys' fees, in connection with the enforcement of this Agreement." The complaint marks the bolded italic passages with "(Emphasis added)." The "***" marks are in the complaint itself, showing where it cut text out of the section.
remedy_named: "Demand Repayment of Grant Funds," Section 9(b)(ii). Not called a clawback and not called liquidated damages. The section heading in Section 5(c) is "Remedy" and the Section 9(b) heading is "Effect of Breach; Remedies." Section 9(e) adds attorney fees.
agreement_is_exhibit: Yes. Both the 2019 Grant Agreement (Exhibit 1) and the 2020 Amended and Restated Grant Agreement (Exhibit 2) are attached in full, along with the two demand letters as Exhibits 3 and 4. The filed complaint PDF runs 27 pages: pages 1 to 6 are the complaint, the remainder are the exhibits. This is the opposite of the Olive AI case, where JobsOhio withheld the agreement on confidentiality grounds.
outcome: Voluntarily dismissed with prejudice by JobsOhio. The filing reads in full: "Now comes Plaintiff JobsOhio and hereby dismisses this action with prejudice." It gives no reason and states no payment. No judgment was ever entered and no answer was ever filed. The clerk terminated the case the same day with Supreme Court termination code 08. Service on the company at the Canton address was completed 2025-10-30; a parallel mailing to Harvard Business Services in Lewes, Delaware was refused.
amount_recovered: Not stated. No filing states any sum paid. A dismissal with prejudice is not a satisfaction of judgment and no dollar figure appears anywhere in it. Do not infer a recovery.

notes: Three things stand out. First, JobsOhio attached the whole grant agreement here, so the full contract text is on the public record in this case, unlike Olive AI where it refused to attach it. Second, the gap between the demand and the suit: two letters demanded $200,000, the complaint demanded $1,250,000, the entire disbursement, on the theory that failing to pay the $200,000 was itself a breach entitling JobsOhio to everything. Third, the repayment remedy is discretionary on its face. Section 9(b)(ii) says Grantor 'may demand repayment of all or a portion of Grant Funds disbursed,' which leaves the amount to JobsOhio. The company reached 137 of 250 jobs, about 55 percent, and 57 percent of the payroll target, and was sued for 100 percent of the money. Judge Andria C. Noble. Plaintiff's counsel Robert J. Mann and Mary Spahia-Carducci of Mann & Carducci Co. LPA, the same firm as in the Olive AI contract suit. I read the complaint and the dismissal in full. I did not read the attached agreements themselves page by page, pages 7 to 27 of the complaint PDF; the quoted sections above come from the complaint's own block quotes.

notes: The important finding here is that the trigger was a missing form. JobsOhio sued for the entire $300,000 because the company did not turn in its 2023 Annual Report, and pleaded the metric shortfall only on information and belief. The agreement text bears this out: Section 6(b) says failing to file any Annual Report "shall be a default," and Section 9(a)(iii) makes a reporting failure a Breach, which unlocks Section 9(b)(ii) repayment of all funds. In this version of the template, unlike Nidec's, Section 9(a)(iii) has no cure period. The complaint puts the (Emphasis added) marker on the reporting clause, showing JobsOhio was leaning on it. Dismissed without prejudice about five months later with no explanation on the record.

notes: The agreement text is not identical across cases, and this is where it shows. Nidec's Section 9(a)(iii) and 9(a)(iv) both read "Grantee fails, after being provided a reasonable time to cure," a cure right that is absent from the same clauses in the Union Metal and American Nuts agreements. Each company negotiates its own terms; there is no single JobsOhio grant agreement. On the merits this is the starkest shortfall in the batch: zero of 29 new jobs, zero of $2,149,000 in new payroll, and retained payroll about 7 percent short. The case lasted 22 days from complaint to dismissal with prejudice, which suggests a resolution reached off the record, but nothing in the file says so and no amount appears. Grant funds of $200,000 match the Form 990 figure for the 2020 grant year.
